verdict.summary:
Round 6 is a comment-only change (24735e51) that resolves round 5's sole finding: the top-of-arm comment in recognise_spatial now scopes its "residual FILTER remains authoritative" claim, exempting the within-region orientations an installed provider may certify exactly. It matches the two comments that follow it (SpatialKind::within_region doc and the struct-literal comment), so the file no longer asserts an invariant that would make a future sixth orientation with within_region:true look safe. No findings this round.

Re-verified the whole change by running it, not by reading alone.

Soundness: each shape is decided in exactly one place. Block 1 matches only WITHIN/INTERSECTS variable-first; the new match's arm 1 requires the variable SECOND, arm 2 requires CONTAINS variable-first, so the sets are disjoint and no shape is routed twice. sfContains(?g,?h) hits arm 1 and returns None via `?` (arm 2 would also have failed), so no recognition is lost to arm ordering. Both-constant and arity!=2 fall through to None. within_region is true only for sfContains(REGION,?g) == within(?g,REGION); the four converse/intersects orientations get false and keep the residual geof: FILTER. within(REGION,?g) and contains(?g,REGION) imply AABB intersection, so the bbox scan is a valid superset for them.

Provider contract: bbox_candidate_literals uses locate_in_envelope_intersecting (index.rs:711) — true AABB intersection, not a containment window — so a geometry strictly containing the region IS returned. lib.rs and SKILL.md now state that obligation explicitly.
